title: Notes on Partial Differential Equations
author: John K. Hunter
locator: Section 6.A.3, Theorem 6.35, printed p.203 (PDF p.209), equation (6.43)
text_kind: paraphrase of independently read theorem, not a Lean-derived target
text: Let X be a Banach space and let f belong to L1(0,T;X). The function f has an integrable weak derivative g if and only if there is a constant c0 such that f(t)=c0+integral_0^t g(s) ds for almost every t. In this case the strong derivative exists almost everywhere and agrees with g.
qualifications: The derivative g is the actual weak derivative of f, not an arbitrary unrelated function.
The source asserts almost-everywhere differentiability; no everywhere-at-zero upgrade is attributed to the source.
Continuous weak derivative yields pointwise differentiability by the fundamental theorem, but that corollary is not represented as an original quotation.
